So, in this game you play as Mick Carter, [i]a drifter[/i], who has clearly had better weeks. No job. No plan. No clean clothes. Basically, you'll be playing a man whose life fits neatly into a single grocery bag. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3630499900

You wake up on a train like your life derailed somewhere between yesterday and now. [i]Possibly earlier.[/i] Immediately you'll notice that Mick narrates everything like he is stuck inside his own gritty novel. He does not just open a door. He'll narrate [i]"I give the door a push. It does not move. Figures."[/i] It feels like he is always roleplaying his own life, even when nothing impressive is happening, and I love it. The voice acting is awesome and carries a huge part of the experience. Every line sounds natural, I actually felt like the actors understand who these people are instead of just reading words off a screen. Micks delivery is especially strong. Shoutout to Mick [i]~Wooooo![/i] His dry tone and tired sarcasm made him a very enjoyable character to play.

From the start the 'drifter' vibe makes you feel like someone who fell out of the world and landed back in it sideways. The game leans into that feeling of being unwanted and out of place and it works. You are not a hero. You are just a hobo trying to survive the trouble that found him. But slowly the story slips into something stranger. At first you're just someone who's at the wrong place at the wrong time. Then slowly you'll start realizing this is not [i]just[/i] a rough story about a guy at the bottom.

The mystery turns Lovecraftian and unsettling in a really good way. Not with jump scares. It eases you into it until you suddenly notice you are deeply hooked into what is going on. What really surprised me is how the ending landed emotionally for me. After all the tension, the paranoia and strange horror... the game quietly turns toward [spoiler][b]L♡VE [/b][/spoiler] ([i]Not in a cheesy way[/I]). Both sides of the story are driven by it. The hero. The villain. Different paths, same problem. It becomes the reason things started and the reason they end. It reframes everything that came before without spelling it out. In a way, even for the villain, it's touching.

You've probably already noticed the pixel art. I can only say, [i]yes yes yeees![/i] The pixel art looks fantastic from start to finish. Every location feels deliberate and the artists know exactly how to use light and color to set a tone. Though, there are quite a few moments where the game fades to black to narrate what happens instead of animating it. Most of the time this works well. It keeps the pacing tight and lets your imagination fill in the gaps. In a few key scenes though, I found myself wishing the game stayed on screen a little longer. Seeing some moments play out would have hit harder I think.

[b]Steam Deck:[/b] Perfect for the Steam Deck! The controls feel fully designed for a controller instead of those games that are awkwardly mapped after the fact. For a lack of better words, there is a.. uh... radial targeting system? Just take it from me, they have implemented an especially smart way to handle point-and-click-ing with a controller and makes interacting with the world feel fast and natural.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3630500982

[b]♡ Highly recommended ♡.[/b] If you like story driven games with sharp writing and incredible voice-acting, you will most likely enjoy this one. [b]I hope to see more from this team!![/b]
